name: All the Weight of Open Sky
description: A documentary assembled from smuggled footage, whistleblower testimony, and hacked medical records exposing the Vela Consortium's decade-long program of non-consensual BCI modification trials conducted on Tier 1 residents in the Gray Zone's northern wards — marketed to subjects as 'cognitive assistance programs.' The film was compiled by an anonymous collective calling itself the Oversight and has never been officially released; it exists entirely on pirate mesh networks and dead-drop physical media. Runtime is 3 hours and 14 minutes and contains unedited medical procedure footage.
cultural_impact: Became the foundational document of the Gray Zone BCI Rights movement, and the Oversight collective's anonymous mesh signal — three short tones — became a recognition code among activists and underground medics.
story_hooks: A Vela security team is tracking down every node that has hosted the film; one of those nodes belongs to someone the players care about.

One of the documentary's subjects — a modified the Gray Zone resident — has begun experiencing the film's footage as recovered memory rather than as something they're watching, suggesting their BCI contains more than they know.
The Oversight collective wants to release a second film and needs the players to extract a Vela research physician who is willing to testify on camera — from inside a Vela arcology.
